title: Complete Detector Records and Contextual Source Laws in a Retrocausal Spin Model
abstract: Detector outcome probabilities can be independent of a later measurement setting even when earlier timestamps, detector seeds, or environmental records depend on that setting. We characterize complete-record preservation for a positive wrapped-Cauchy retrocausal spin source. An antipodal identity yields necessary and sufficient conditions for passive and environmental readouts, and source compensation permits a common normalized analyzer for source spins and prepared continuations. Gaussian controller and reset calculations distinguish inverse raw history weights from normalized thermal operations. A quantum instrument provides an operational benchmark, whereas a setting-dependent separable source produces setting-dependent statistics at an earlier joint probe. For two equal-width contexts, a calibrated weak probe requires a minimum source change of $\operatorname{sech}(2g)/8$ in trace distance for exact protection at every nonzero strength. The signal--source-change tradeoff is sharp for this pair of contexts. A contextual positive-history construction recovers the isolated hidden law and preserves records for a specified class of finite adaptive quantum apparatuses, subject to quantum calibration and restricted field access. Direct readout of an added likelihood field distinguishes two future axes with unit probability. The analytical results are supported by continuous-angle and quantum-trajectory simulations, deterministic quadrature, and exhaustive enumeration of a finite policy class. The analysis concerns the specified statistical models; their microscopic physical realization remains an open question.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously analyzes retrocausal spin models to determine the conditions for 'complete detector records' when measurements are context-dependent. It derives mathematical constraints showing when detector outcomes can be independent of future settings despite past records depending on them. The work provides a detailed statistical characterization of information preservation in such non-standard quantum temporal settings.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the conditions under which detector outcome probabilities in a retrocausal spin model can remain independent of later measurement settings, even when earlier detector records depend on those settings.
main_result: It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for passive readouts and provides a contextual embedding that recovers the isolated hidden law for specified finite adaptive quantum apparatuses.
method: The analysis combines theoretical derivations using Fourier series, theorems based on antipodal symmetry, and numerical simulations across various contexts.
model_or_system: The model is a retrocausal spin source characterized as a positive wrapped-Cauchy source, involving measurements on spin angles ($\lambda$) and outcomes ($a, b$). It analyzes the consistency of detector records across time-like measurements.
key_observables: Detector outcome probabilities $P(dr | x, a, y)$, corrected history measures $\mathrm{e}P(d\lambda, a, dr, b)$, and the signal--source-change tradeoff.
important_parameters: Source widths ($\gamma_A, \gamma_B$), coupling strengths ($g$), and the measurement settings ($x, y$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to specified statistical models, and the microscopic physical realization of the source-field interaction remains an open question.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of detector records on subsequent analyzer axes ($y$) for various parameters, showing agreement probabilities and mean outcome-seed products.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining record consistency, deriving conditions for passive readouts using symmetry theorems, developing corrected history measures, and finally applying these concepts to quantum instrument benchmarks and numerical simulations.
why_interesting: The deep focus on retrocausality, contextuality, and the mathematical constraints on information flow touches upon fundamental questions in quantum foundations, which often intersect with open quantum systems theory.
